name: Apiculture queen detection / hive inspection
open_problem: Beekeepers must manually open hives and inspect frames to confirm the queen is present and laying; her loss can collapse a colony, but inspection is intrusive, time-consuming, weather-limited, and depends on the beekeeper's eye for spotting a single bee or fresh eggs among thousands.
verbatim_quote: Manual inspections are laborious and disruptive, motivating the need for automated, non-invasive detection methods.

name: Varroa mite monitoring (alcohol wash / sugar roll)
open_problem: To decide whether to treat for varroa, beekeepers take a ~300-bee sample, dislodge mites with alcohol or powdered sugar, and count mites by hand against seasonal thresholds; counting is tedious, error-prone, kills the sample (alcohol), and is done by feel/eye rather than any automated sensor.
verbatim_quote: The powdered sugar roll is currently the most common and quickest tool to monitor mites.

name: Sericulture cocoon grading and silk reeling
open_problem: Silk quality depends on grading cocoons and reeling filament from them, traditionally judged by experienced workers by eye/feel (shell ratio, defects, seasonal quality); the larva must be killed at the chrysalis stage before the moth breaks the filament, and grading remains a hands-on craft.
verbatim_quote: Because an emerging moth would break the cocoon filament, the larva is killed in the cocoon by steam or hot air at the chrysalis stage.

name: Orphan / underutilized crop breeding
open_problem: Neglected crops vital to smallholders (e.g. fonio, bambara groundnut, teff) have almost no genomic or breeding resources and little institutional data; improvement is done with minimal investment and lost institutional memory, far behind wheat/rice/maize.
verbatim_quote: Orphan crops are also known as underutilized crops, neglected crops or crops for the future, named for the lack of genetic improvement, not for lack of use or incorporation into cultural diets.

name: Agroforestry / alley cropping design
open_problem: Designing tree-crop alley systems requires predicting decades of light/water/nutrient competition between rows of trees and alley crops, but interactions are poorly characterized and the long time horizon means design is largely by rule-of-thumb and farmer judgment.
verbatim_quote: As trees and shrubs grow, they influence light, water and nutrient regimes in the field, and these interactions are what sets alley cropping apart from more common monocropping systems.

name: Seed saving: roguing and isolation
open_problem: Keeping a landrace/heirloom variety true-to-type requires the saver to recognize and remove off-type plants (roguing) before pollination and to maintain isolation distances; this is judgment-by-eye over whole populations with essentially no decision-support tooling.
verbatim_quote: Roguing is the process of removing weak or "off-type" plants before they spread their pollen.

name: Soil judging / field texture-by-feel
open_problem: Classifying a soil in the field (texture, clay/sand percentage, horizons) is done by hand-feel ribboning and color books in a pit, a tacit skill built by practice; there is no portable instrument that replaces the trained fingers used in soil/land judging.
verbatim_quote: In the field, it is necessary to estimate the soil texture by feeling it with the fingers, a skill that can be developed with practice and will be used in contests.

name: Polynesian wayfinding (star compass & wave piloting)
open_problem: Traditional navigators cross open Pacific ocean with no instruments, holding course by a memorized 32-house star compass and reading swell patterns/refraction off islands entirely in the head; the knowledge is oral, hard to teach, and has no computational model.
verbatim_quote: The star compass is a mental construct and not physical like a western compass.

name: Inuit snow/wind (sastrugi) wayfinding
open_problem: Arctic travelers orient in whiteouts and on featureless sea ice by reading wind-carved snow ridges (sastrugi), named prevailing winds, ice sounds, and animal cues; this is a multi-sensory tacit skill with no GPS-independent tooling that captures it.
verbatim_quote: The snowdrifts left by prevailing winds are the most reliable source of spatial orientation, and only the drifts left by prevailing winds can last throughout the winter.

name: Maritime pilotage (local-knowledge ship handling)
open_problem: Harbour/river pilots con large ships through dangerous waterways using visual references and intimate local knowledge of tides, currents, silting and shoals not shown on charts; this expertise is tacit, firsthand, and resists codification.
verbatim_quote: A maritime pilot is a mariner who has specific knowledge of an often dangerous or congested waterway, such as harbors or river mouths.

name: Orienteering route choice / map-terrain matching
open_problem: Orienteers must continuously match a topographic map to terrain while moving at speed and choose among routes weighing distance, climb, vegetation and footing; route choice and proactive map-reading are cognitive skills with little algorithmic support for the runner.
verbatim_quote: A handrail is defined as a linear feature on a map that parallels your route and can be used as a quick aid to navigating yourself to the next control.

name: Cave navigation & survey (compass/clinometer/tape)
open_problem: Underground there is no GPS and no map until someone makes one; cavers find their way and build surveys leg-by-leg with magnetic compass, clinometer and tape, fighting magnetic interference, reading error and slowness, often relying on a guideline to find the way out.
verbatim_quote: The DistoX2 unit is a beefed-up laser rangefinder used to measure the distance and direction between survey stations underground.

name: Dead reckoning (manual position keeping)
open_problem: When fixes are unavailable, navigators advance a known position by hand from logged speed, heading and time; errors accumulate (~10-15% of distance) until a fix lets them reinitialize, and the running plot is maintained manually by the navigator's feel.
verbatim_quote: The errors that are inherent in dead reckoning accumulate; when a position has been checked, the reckoning is therefore generally restarted from that position.

name: Desert wayfinding (Tuareg/Bedouin dune navigation)
open_problem: Desert nomads cross shifting sand seas by recognizing slow-moving dune systems, named dunes, rock formations, sun and stars, with routes and dune names taught orally; the landscape changes with wind and the skill lives only in inherited memory.
verbatim_quote: While the wind in the desert is constantly changing the landscape, the big dune systems are moving very slowly, so they are more recognizable and can be used as landmarks.
